in deploy/yantrik-os/yos-mcp are the same table written twice, on purpose:
the bridge deciding for itself costs one read of the shell instead of two.
Two copies drift. These vectors are what stops it being silent — the Rust
side writes them and a test asserts the file still matches; the Python side
is driven through every one of them by yos-mcp-selftest.py.
layer: `shell` came straight out of Modes::decide. `harness_cap` is
YOS_MCP_MAX_PERMISSION, which the shell does not enforce and should not —
it is a cap a harness puts on itself — and `browser` is the plan-mode rule
for tools that are not on the shell's surface at all. Both are modelled in
the generator, which the generator says so about.
recoverable is carried and is expected to change nothing: it decides
whether a session rule may be MADE (approvals::may_offer_session_rule), and
neither decision table looks at it. A vector where it starts to matter is a

outcomes.run: ran; nobody was asked and nothing is written down
outcomes.run_logged: ran unasked; `ask` mode would have raised a card, so it goes in the audit
outcomes.ask: a card in front of the person, and a wait
outcomes.refuse_grade: the grade is not one this OS defines; None is not safe
outcomes.refuse_ceiling: above tool_permission; nobody is asked, in any mode
outcomes.refuse_mode: plan mode: nothing was changed, say what you would do
